1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z\"\u003e\u003c/path\u003e\u003c/svg\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eThe user of this tool is not a human. It's an LLM.\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003educktel is a lightweight local OpenTelemetry backend. It receives OTLP traces, logs, and metrics over HTTP, stores them as partitioned Parquet files, and makes them queryable via embedded DuckDB through a CLI.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eSingle binary. No external dependencies. No dashboards. No alerting infrastructure. No webhooks. No notification channels.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eAn LLM agent shells out to \u003ccode\u003educktel query\u003c/code\u003e, gets structured JSON back, and reasons about the results. The agent \u003cem\u003eis\u003c/em\u003e the dashboard. The agent \u003cem\u003eis\u003c/em\u003e the alerting engine. The agent \u003cem\u003eis\u003c/em\u003e the intelligence layer. Everything ducktel does is designed for that consumer — not for a human staring at a screen.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"markdown-heading\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ch2 tabindex=\"-1\" class=\"heading-element\" dir=\"auto\"\u003eWhy This Exists\u003c/h2\u003e\u003ca id=\"user-content-why-this-exists\" class=\"anchor\" aria-label=\"Permalink: Why This Exists\" href=\"#why-this-exists\"\u003e\u003csvg data-component=\"Octicon\" class=\"octicon octicon-link\" viewBox=\"0 0 16 16\" version=\"1.1\" width=\"16\" height=\"16\" aria-hidden=\"true\"\u003e\u003cpath d=\"m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z\"\u003e\u003c/path\u003e\u003c/svg\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eThe observability industry is undergoing a huge disruption. A fundamental compression of the value chain that will reshape how software is monitored and debugged.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eFor the past decade, observability platforms have monetized three layers: \u003cstrong\u003eingestion\u003c/strong\u003e (getting telemetry data in), \u003cstrong\u003estorage\u003c/strong\u003e (keeping it queryable), and \u003cstrong\u003eintelligence\u003c/strong\u003e (helping humans understand it). Vendors like Datadog, Dynatrace, and Splunk built billion-dollar businesses by bundling all three behind proprietary formats, query languages, and dashboards.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eThat bundle is coming apart.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"markdown-heading\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ch3 tabindex=\"-1\" class=\"heading-element\" dir=\"auto\"\u003eThe forces at work\u003c/h3\u003e\u003ca id=\"user-content-the-forces-at-work\" class=\"anchor\" aria-label=\"Permalink: The forces at work\" href=\"#the-forces-at-work\"\u003e\u003csvg data-component=\"Octicon\" class=\"octicon octicon-link\" viewBox=\"0 0 16 16\" version=\"1.1\" width=\"16\" height=\"16\" aria-hidden=\"true\"\u003e\u003cpath d=\"m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z\"\u003e\u003c/path\u003e\u003c/svg\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eFrom below, storage is commoditizing.\u003c/strong\u003e OpenTelemetry standardized the wire format. Parquet and Iceberg standardized columnar storage. DuckDB, ClickHouse, and object stores like S3 made it trivially cheap to store and query telemetry at scale. The marginal cost of storing a GB of logs is collapsing toward $0.023/month. When storage is a commodity, charging $2.50/GB for ingestion becomes indefensible — and enterprises are noticing. Research shows 96% of organizations are actively taking steps to control observability costs, with 70% focused on optimizing existing spend rather than expanding.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eFrom above, AI is eating the intelligence layer.\u003c/strong\u003e LLMs can write SQL. They can scan billions of log lines, correlate traces with metrics, perform root cause analysis, and define SLOs by analyzing historical patterns — all in seconds. They don't need dashboards, proprietary query languages, or pre-built visualizations. Give an LLM access to raw telemetry in an open format and a SQL interface, and it replicates what took observability platforms years and thousands of engineers to build.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eThe emerging stack looks like this:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"snippet-clipboard-content notranslate position-relative overflow-auto\" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content=\"OpenTelemetry SDKs → Commodity columnar storage → AI agent\"\u003e\u003cpre class=\"notranslate\"\u003e\u003ccode\u003eOpenTelemetry SDKs → Commodity columnar storage → AI agent\n\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/pre\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eEverything in between — the dashboards, the query builders, the alert rule editors, the visualization layers — becomes optional middleware. Not immediately worthless, but structurally threatened.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"markdown-heading\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ch3 tabindex=\"-1\" class=\"heading-element\" dir=\"auto\"\u003eWhat gets replaced\u003c/h3\u003e\u003ca id=\"user-content-what-gets-replaced\" class=\"anchor\" aria-label=\"Permalink: What gets replaced\" href=\"#what-gets-replaced\"\u003e\u003csvg data-component=\"Octicon\" class=\"octicon octicon-link\" viewBox=\"0 0 16 16\" version=\"1.1\" width=\"16\" height=\"16\" aria-hidden=\"true\"\u003e\u003cpath d=\"m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z\"\u003e\u003c/path\u003e\u003c/svg\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eTraditional observability platforms provide value through:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cul dir=\"auto\"\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eDashboards\u003c/strong\u003e → AI generates purpose-built visualizations on demand, used for a single investigation, then discarded. Persistent dashboards are artifacts of human cognitive limitation, not engineering necessity.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eQuery languages\u003c/strong\u003e → AI writes SQL (or whatever the storage engine speaks). Proprietary query languages like LogQL, PromQL, and SPL become friction, not features.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eAlert rules\u003c/strong\u003e → AI performs continuous inference against raw data, identifying anomalies contextually rather than through static thresholds that humans forgot to update.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eRoot cause analysis\u003c/strong\u003e → AI traces causality across all three signal types natively, joining traces to logs to metrics without requiring humans to manually correlate.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eSLO definition\u003c/strong\u003e → AI analyzes historical patterns, understands user impact, and sets thresholds that actually reflect system behavior rather than guesses.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"markdown-heading\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ch3 tabindex=\"-1\" class=\"heading-element\" dir=\"auto\"\u003eWhat remains\u003c/h3\u003e\u003ca id=\"user-content-what-remains\" class=\"anchor\" aria-label=\"Permalink: What remains\" href=\"#what-remains\"\u003e\u003csvg data-component=\"Octicon\" class=\"octicon octicon-link\" viewBox=\"0 0 16 16\" version=\"1.1\" width=\"16\" height=\"16\" aria-hidden=\"true\"\u003e\u003cpath d=\"m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z\"\u003e\u003c/path\u003e\u003c/svg\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eIngest and store. That's it. You need something to receive telemetry and something to persist it in a queryable format. Everything above that layer is intelligence — and intelligence is exactly what LLMs do.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003educktel is a proof of concept for this thesis.\u003c/strong\u003e It is the minimal backend an AI agent needs to do observability: receive OTLP, write Parquet, expose SQL. No dashboards. No query language. No visualization engine. Just structured data and a query interface that any LLM can use by shelling out to a CLI.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"markdown-heading\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ch2 tabindex=\"-1\" class=\"heading-element\" dir=\"auto\"\u003eDesign Principles\u003c/h2\u003e\u003ca id=\"user-content-design-principles\" class=\"anchor\" aria-label=\"Permalink: Design Principles\" href=\"#design-principles\"\u003e\u003csvg data-component=\"Octicon\" class=\"octicon octicon-link\" viewBox=\"0 0 16 16\" version=\"1.1\" width=\"16\" height=\"16\" aria-hidden=\"true\"\u003e\u003cpath d=\"m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z\"\u003e\u003c/path\u003e\u003c/svg\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eOTel-native.\u003c/strong\u003e ducktel speaks OTLP/HTTP natively — both protobuf and JSON. No proprietary agents, no custom SDKs, no vendor lock-in at the collection layer. If your application is instrumented with OpenTelemetry, ducktel accepts it unchanged.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eParquet-first storage.\u003c/strong\u003e Telemetry is flushed to date-partitioned Parquet files. Parquet is columnar, compressed, and universally supported. DuckDB, Spark, Pandas, Polars, and dozens of other tools can read it natively. Your data never gets trapped in a proprietary format.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eSQL is the interface.\u003c/strong\u003e Every query goes through DuckDB's SQL engine. This is a deliberate choice — SQL is the most widely understood query language on earth, and more importantly, it's the language LLMs are best at generating. No proprietary DSL to learn, no query builder to click through.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eCLI-first, agent-friendly.\u003c/strong\u003e ducktel is designed to be called from a shell. An LLM agent investigating an incident can shell out to \u003ccode\u003educktel query\u003c/code\u003e, get structured JSON back, reason about the results, and issue follow-up queries. The entire diagnostic loop — from anomaly detection to root cause analysis — can happen programmatically without a human touching a browser.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eSingle binary, zero dependencies.\u003c/strong\u003e \u003ccode\u003ego build\u003c/code\u003e and you have everything. No databases to run, no message queues to configure, no clusters to manage. This matters for local development, CI/CD pipelines, edge deployments, and anywhere you want telemetry without the overhead of a platform.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eNothing is dropped.\u003c/strong\u003e All OTLP fields are preserved in the Parquet schema. Resource attributes, scope metadata, span events, links, exemplars — everything. The schema is wide because the data model is rich, and AI agents can use all of it.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"markdown-heading\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ch2 tabindex=\"-1\" It's not trying to be Grafana. It's not trying to be a platform at all.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eIt's an answer to a question: *What's the minimum viable backend when the consumer of telemetry is an AI agent instead of a human?\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eThe answer turns out to be surprisingly small. An OTLP receiver, a Parquet writer, and a SQL engine. That's the whole thing. Everything observability platforms spent a decade building on top of that foundation — the dashboards, the query builders, the alerting engines, the visualization layers — was scaffolding for human cognition. Necessary scaffolding, when humans were the ones interpreting telemetry. But scaffolding nonetheless.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eWhen an LLM can write SQL, read structured output, reason about distributed systems, and iterate on queries faster than any human can click through a UI — the scaffolding becomes overhead.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eThis isn't a prediction about the distant future. The pieces exist today. OpenTelemetry standardized collection. Parquet and DuckDB commoditized storage and query. LLMs can do the reasoning. ducktel just wires them together in the simplest possible way and gets out of the road.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"markdown-heading\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ch2 tabindex=\"-1\" class=\"heading-element\" dir=\"auto\"\u003eStatus\u003c/h2\u003e\u003ca id=\"user-content-status\" class=\"anchor\" aria-label=\"Permalink: Status\" href=\"#status\"\u003e\u003csvg data-component=\"Octicon\" class=\"octicon octicon-link\" viewBox=\"0 0 16 16\" version=\"1.1\" width=\"16\" height=\"16\" aria-hidden=\"true\"\u003e\u003cpath d=\"m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z\"\u003e\u003c/path\u003e\u003c/svg\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eEarly stage. ducktel","","**The user of this tool is not a human. It's an LLM.**","","ducktel is a lightweight local OpenTelemetry backend. It receives OTLP traces, logs, and metrics over HTTP, stores them as partitioned Parquet files, and makes them queryable via embedded DuckDB through a CLI.","","Single binary. No external dependencies. No dashboards. No alerting infrastructure. No webhooks. No notification channels.","","An LLM agent shells out to `ducktel query`, gets structured JSON back, and reasons about the results. The agent *is* the dashboard. The agent *is* the alerting engine. The agent *is* the intelligence layer. Everything ducktel does is designed for that consumer — not for a human staring at a screen.","","## Why This Exists","","The observability industry is undergoing a huge disruption. A fundamental compression of the value chain that will reshape how software is monitored and debugged.","","For the past decade, observability platforms have monetized three layers: **ingestion** (getting telemetry data in), **storage** (keeping it queryable), and **intelligence** (helping humans understand it). Vendors like Datadog, Dynatrace, and Splunk built billion-dollar businesses by bundling all three behind proprietary formats, query languages, and dashboards.","","That bundle is coming apart.","","### The forces at work","","**From below, storage is commoditizing.** OpenTelemetry standardized the wire format. Parquet and Iceberg standardized columnar storage. DuckDB, ClickHouse, and object stores like S3 made it trivially cheap to store and query telemetry at scale. The marginal cost of storing a GB of logs is collapsing toward $0.023/month. When storage is a commodity, charging $2.50/GB for ingestion becomes indefensible — and enterprises are noticing. Research shows 96% of organizations are actively taking steps to control observability costs, with 70% focused on optimizing existing spend rather than expanding.","","**From above, AI is eating the intelligence layer.** LLMs can write SQL. They can scan billions of log lines, correlate traces with metrics, perform root cause analysis, and define SLOs by analyzing historical patterns — all in seconds. They don't need dashboards, proprietary query languages, or pre-built visualizations. Give an LLM access to raw telemetry in an open format and a SQL interface, and it replicates what took observability platforms years and thousands of engineers to build.","","The emerging stack looks like this:","","```","OpenTelemetry SDKs → Commodity columnar storage → AI agent","```","","Everything in between — the dashboards, the query builders, the alert rule editors, the visualization layers — becomes optional middleware. Not immediately worthless, but structurally threatened.","","### What gets replaced","","Traditional observability platforms provide value through:","","- **Dashboards** → AI generates purpose-built visualizations on demand, used for a single investigation, then discarded. Persistent dashboards are artifacts of human cognitive limitation, not engineering necessity.","- **Query languages** → AI writes SQL (or whatever the storage engine speaks). Proprietary query languages like LogQL, PromQL, and SPL become friction, not features.","- **Alert rules** → AI performs continuous inference against raw data, identifying anomalies contextually rather than through static thresholds that humans forgot to update.","- **Root cause analysis** → AI traces causality across all three signal types natively, joining traces to logs to metrics without requiring humans to manually correlate.","- **SLO definition** → AI analyzes historical patterns, understands user impact, and sets thresholds that actually reflect system behavior rather than guesses.","","### What remains","","Ingest and store. That's it. You need something to receive telemetry and something to persist it in a queryable format. Everything above that layer is intelligence — and intelligence is exactly what LLMs do.","","**ducktel is a proof of concept for this thesis.** It is the minimal backend an AI agent needs to do observability: receive OTLP, write Parquet, expose SQL. No dashboards. No query language. No visualization engine. Just structured data and a query interface that any LLM can use by shelling out to a CLI.","","## Design Principles","","**OTel-native.** ducktel speaks OTLP/HTTP natively — both protobuf and JSON. No proprietary agents, no custom SDKs, no vendor lock-in at the collection layer. If your application is instrumented with OpenTelemetry, ducktel accepts it unchanged.","","**Parquet-first storage.** Telemetry is flushed to date-partitioned Parquet files. Parquet is columnar, compressed, and universally supported. DuckDB, Spark, Pandas, Polars, and dozens of other tools can read it natively. Your data never gets trapped in a proprietary format.","","**SQL is the interface.** Every query goes through DuckDB's SQL engine. This is a deliberate choice — SQL is the most widely understood query language on earth, and more importantly, it's the language LLMs are best at generating. No proprietary DSL to learn, no query builder to click through.","","**CLI-first, agent-friendly.** ducktel is designed to be called from a shell. An LLM agent investigating an incident can shell out to `ducktel query`, get structured JSON back, reason about the results, and issue follow-up queries. The entire diagnostic loop — from anomaly detection to root cause analysis — can happen programmatically without a human touching a browser.","","**Single binary, zero dependencies.** `go build` and you have everything. No databases to run, no message queues to configure, no clusters to manage. This matters for local development, CI/CD pipelines, edge deployments, and anywhere you want telemetry without the overhead of a platform.","","**Nothing is dropped.** All OTLP fields are preserved in the Parquet schema. Resource attributes, scope metadata, span events, links, exemplars — everything. The schema is wide because the data model is rich, and AI agents can use all of it.","","## Architecture","","```","┌──────────────────────┐","│   OTel-instrumented  │","│     applications     │","└──────────┬───────────┘","           │ OTLP/HTTP (protobuf or JSON)","           ▼","┌──────────────────────┐","│    ducktel serve     │","│                      │","│  ┌────────────────┐  │","│  │ OTLP Receiver  │  │","│  │ /v1/traces     │  │","│  │ /v1/logs       │  │","│  │ /v1/metrics    │  │","│  └───────┬────────┘  │","│          ▼           │","│  ┌────────────────┐  │","│  │ Memory Buffer  │  │","│  │ + Flush Timer  │  │","│  └───────┬────────┘  │","│          ▼           │","│  ┌────────────────┐  │","│  │ Parquet Writer │  │","│  └────────────────┘  │","└──────────────────────┘","           │","           ▼","┌──────────────────────┐","│   data/              │","│   ├── traces/        │","│   │   └── YYYY-MM-DD │","│   ├── logs/          │","│   │   └── YYYY-MM-DD │","│   └── metrics/       │","│       └── YYYY-MM-DD │","└──────────┬───────────┘","           │","           ▼","┌──────────────────────┐","│   ducktel query      │","│   ducktel traces     │","│   ducktel logs       │     ◄── LLM agents shell out here","│   ducktel metrics    │","│                      │","│  ┌────────────────┐  │","│  │ Embedded       │  │","│  │ DuckDB         │  │","│  │ (Parquet glob) │  │","│  └────────────────┘  │","└──────────────────────┘","```","","## Install","","```bash","go install github.com/davidgeorgehope/ducktel/cmd/ducktel@latest","```","","Or build from source:","","```bash","git clone https://github.com/davidgeorgehope/ducktel.git","cd ducktel","go build -o ducktel ./cmd/ducktel/","```","","## Usage","","### Start the collector","","```bash","ducktel serve","```","","Listens on `:4318` for OTLP/HTTP (protobuf and JSON). Accepts all three signal types:","","- `POST /v1/traces`","- `POST /v1/logs`","- `POST /v1/metrics`","","Data is buffered in memory and flushed to Parquet files under `./data/{traces,logs,metrics}/YYYY-MM-DD/`.","","Options:","","```","--port            Port to listen on (default 4318)","--flush-interval  How often to flush to disk (default 30s)","--data-dir        Storage directory (default ./data)","```","","### Query with SQL","","Run arbitrary SQL against any signal type:","","```bash","ducktel query \"SELECT service_name, span_name, duration_ms FROM traces ORDER BY duration_ms DESC LIMIT 10\"","ducktel query \"SELECT severity_text, body FROM logs WHERE severity_text = 'ERROR'\"","ducktel query \"SELECT metric_name, value_double FROM metrics WHERE metric_type = 'gauge'\"","```","","### List services","","```bash","ducktel services","```","","### Browse traces","","```bash","ducktel traces --service my-api --since 1h --status error --limit 50","```","","### Browse logs","","```bash","ducktel logs --service my-api --since 1h --severity error","ducktel logs --search \"timeout\" --limit 100","```","","### Browse metrics","","```bash","ducktel metrics --service my-api --name http.request.duration --type histogram","ducktel metrics --since 30m","```","","### Show schema","","```bash","ducktel schema traces","ducktel schema logs","ducktel schema metrics","```","","### Output formats","","All query commands support `--format json` (default), `--format table`, or `--format csv`:","","```bash","ducktel traces --since 30m --format table","ducktel logs --severity error --format csv","```","","### Saved queries","","Saved queries are the LLM's checklist — queries worth running periodically. ducktel stores them but never executes them automatically. There is no scheduler, no webhook, no notification system. The LLM agent decides when to run them (on its own heartbeat loop, cron, or whenever it wants) and what to do with the results.","","```bash","# Save a query the agent discovered during an investigation","ducktel saved create \"error-rate-by-service\" \\","  \"SELECT service_name, count(*) FILTER (WHERE status_code = 'STATUS_CODE_ERROR') * 100.0 / count(*) as error_pct FROM traces WHERE start_time \u003e= epoch_us(now() - INTERVAL '5 minutes') GROUP BY service_name HAVING error_pct \u003e 0\" \\","  --description \"Error rate by service over last 5 minutes\" \\","  --schedule \"every 60s\" \\","  --tags errors,slo","","# Save a latency check","ducktel saved create \"p99-latency\" \\","  \"SELECT service_name, span_name, quantile_cont(duration_ms, 0.99) as p99_ms FROM traces WHERE start_time \u003e= epoch_us(now() - INTERVAL '10 minutes') GROUP BY service_name, span_name ORDER BY p99_ms DESC LIMIT 10\" \\","  --description \"Top 10 slowest endpoints by P99 latency\" \\","  --schedule \"every 5m\" \\","  --tags latency","","# List all saved queries","ducktel saved list","ducktel saved list --format json","","# Show a specific query's details","ducktel saved show \"error-rate-by-service\"","","# Run a single saved query","ducktel saved run \"error-rate-by-service\"","","# Run ALL saved queries at once — the agent's heartbeat check","# One command, all diagnostics, structured JSON output","ducktel saved run-all","","# Delete a query that's no longer relevant","ducktel saved delete \"error-rate-by-service\"","```","","The `run-all` command is the key primitive. An LLM agent on a heartbeat loop runs `ducktel saved run-all`, gets back a JSON array of all results, and reasons about what needs attention. The investigative query that found a bug today becomes the monitoring query that catches it tomorrow — no translation layer, no alert rule syntax, just SQL.","","## Agent Integration","","ducktel is built for LLM agents. Here's how an agent might investigate an incident:","","```bash","# Step 1: What services are reporting?","ducktel services --format json","","# Step 2: Any errors in the last hour?","ducktel query \"","  SELECT service_name, count(*) as error_count","  FROM traces","  WHERE status_code = 'STATUS_CODE_ERROR'","    AND start_time \u003e= epoch_us(now() - INTERVAL '1 hour')","  GROUP BY service_name","  ORDER BY error_count DESC","\" --format json","","# Step 3: What's failing in the worst service?","ducktel query \"","  SELECT span_name, count(*) as failures, avg(duration_ms) as avg_duration","  FROM traces","  WHERE service_name = 'payment-service'","    AND status_code = 'STATUS_CODE_ERROR'","    AND start_time \u003e= epoch_us(now() - INTERVAL '1 hour')","  GROUP BY span_name","  ORDER BY failures DESC","\" --format json","","# Step 4: Get a specific failing trace","ducktel query \"","  SELECT span_name, parent_span_id, duration_ms, status_code, attributes","  FROM traces","  WHERE trace_id = '...'","  ORDER BY start_time","\" --format json","","# Step 5: Correlate with logs","ducktel query \"","  SELECT timestamp, severity_text, body","  FROM logs","  WHERE trace_id = '...'","  ORDER BY timestamp","\" --format json","","# Step 6: Check if this is a latency regression","ducktel query \"","  SELECT metric_name, service_name,","         sum / count as avg_ms, max as max_ms","  FROM metrics","  WHERE metric_name = 'http.request.duration'","    AND service_name = 'payment-service'","  ORDER BY timestamp DESC","  LIMIT 20","\" --format json","```","","Every step returns structured JSON. The agent reasons about each result and decides what to query next. No dashboards opened. No humans clicking through UIs. No context-switching between tabs. Just an AI systematically narrowing from \"something's wrong\" to \"here's the root cause and here's the evidence.\"","","This is what observability looks like when the consumer of telemetry is an LLM, not a human staring at a screen.","","### The diagnostic-to-monitoring loop","","The real power of saved queries: the investigative query that diagnosed an incident becomes the monitoring query that prevents the next one. No context switch, no \"now go create an alert rule in a different system.\"","","```bash","# Agent just diagnosed a payment service issue. Save the query that found it:","ducktel saved create \"payment-error-spike\" \\","  \"SELECT count(*) as errors FROM traces WHERE service_name = 'payment-service' AND status_code = 'STATUS_CODE_ERROR' AND start_time \u003e= epoch_us(now() - INTERVAL '5 minutes')\" \\","  --description \"Errors in payment service over 5min window\" \\","  --schedule \"every 60s\" \\","  --tags payment,errors","","# Later, on the agent's heartbeat loop:","ducktel saved run-all","# → Agent sees payment-error-spike returned 0 rows. All three signal types are supported.","","Example OTel Collector config:","","```yaml","exporters:","  otlphttp:","    endpoint: http://localhost:4318","    tls:","      insecure: true","","service:","  pipelines:","    traces:","      exporters: [otlphttp]","    logs:","      exporters: [otlphttp]","    metrics:","      exporters: [otlphttp]","```","","## Example Queries","","```sql","-- Slowest spans in the last hour","SELECT service_name, span_name, duration_ms","FROM traces","WHERE start_time \u003e= epoch_us(now() - INTERVAL '1 hour')","ORDER BY duration_ms DESC","LIMIT 10;","","-- Error rate by service","SELECT service_name,","       count(*) as total,","       count(*) FILTER (WHERE status_code = 'STATUS_CODE_ERROR') as errors","FROM traces","GROUP BY service_name;","","-- Trace waterfall","SELECT span_name, parent_span_id, duration_ms,","       start_time - min(start_time) OVER (PARTITION BY trace_id) as offset_us","FROM traces","WHERE trace_id = '01020304050607080910111213141516'","ORDER BY start_time;","","-- Recent error logs","SELECT timestamp, service_name, body","FROM logs","WHERE severity_text = 'ERROR'","ORDER BY timestamp DESC","LIMIT 20;","","-- Logs correlated with a trace","SELECT severity_text, body","FROM logs","WHERE trace_id = '01020304050607080910111213141516'","ORDER BY timestamp;","","-- P99 request duration from histograms","SELECT metric_name, service_name,","       sum / count as avg_ms,","       max as max_ms","FROM metrics","WHERE metric_name = 'http.request.duration'","ORDER BY timestamp DESC","LIMIT 10;","","-- Cross-signal: find error spans and their logs","SELECT t.span_name, t.duration_ms, l.body","FROM traces t","JOIN logs l ON t.trace_id = l.trace_id AND t.span_id = l.span_id","WHERE t.status_code = 'STATUS_CODE_ERROR'","ORDER BY t.start_time DESC;","```","","## The Bigger Picture","","ducktel isn't trying to be Datadog. It's not trying to be a platform at all.","","It's an answer to a question: *What's the minimum viable backend when the consumer of telemetry is an AI agent instead of a human?","","The answer turns out to be surprisingly small. An OTLP receiver, a Parquet writer, and a SQL engine. That's the whole thing. Everything observability platforms spent a decade building on top of that foundation — the dashboards, the query builders, the alerting engines, the visualization layers — was scaffolding for human cognition. Necessary scaffolding, when humans were the ones interpreting telemetry. But scaffolding nonetheless.","","When an LLM can write SQL, read structured output, reason about distributed systems, and iterate on queries faster than any human can click through a UI — the scaffolding becomes overhead.","","This isn't a prediction about the distant future. The pieces exist today. OpenTelemetry standardized collection. Parquet and DuckDB commoditized storage and query. LLMs can do the reasoning. ducktel just wires them together in the simplest possible way and gets out of the road.","","## Status","","Early stage. The core ingest → store → query loop works. <p dir="auto"><strong>The user of this tool is not a human. It's an LLM.</strong></p>
<p dir="auto">ducktel is a lightweight local OpenTelemetry backend. It receives OTLP traces, logs, and metrics over HTTP, stores them as partitioned Parquet files, and makes them queryable via embedded DuckDB through a CLI.</p>
<p dir="auto">Single binary. No external dependencies. No dashboards. No alerting infrastructure. No webhooks. No notification channels.</p>
<p dir="auto">An LLM agent shells out to <code>ducktel query</code>, gets structured JSON back, and reasons about the results. The agent <em>is</em> the dashboard. The agent <em>is</em> the alerting engine. The agent <em>is</em> the intelligence layer. Everything ducktel does is designed for that consumer — not for a human staring at a screen.</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Why This Exists</h2><a id="user-content-why-this-exists" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Why This Exists" href="#why-this-exists"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">The observability industry is undergoing a huge disruption. A fundamental compression of the value chain that will reshape how software is monitored and debugged.</p>
<p dir="auto">For the past decade, observability platforms have monetized three layers: <strong>ingestion</strong> (getting telemetry data in), <strong>storage</strong> (keeping it queryable), and <strong>intelligence</strong> (helping humans understand it). Vendors like Datadog, Dynatrace, and Splunk built billion-dollar businesses by bundling all three behind proprietary formats, query languages, and dashboards.</p>
<p dir="auto">That bundle is coming apart.</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h3 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">The forces at work</h3><a id="user-content-the-forces-at-work" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: The forces at work" href="#the-forces-at-work"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto"><strong>From below, storage is commoditizing.</strong> OpenTelemetry standardized the wire format. Parquet and Iceberg standardized columnar storage. DuckDB, ClickHouse, and object stores like S3 made it trivially cheap to store and query telemetry at scale. The marginal cost of storing a GB of logs is collapsing toward $0.023/month. When storage is a commodity, charging $2.50/GB for ingestion becomes indefensible — and enterprises are noticing. Research shows 96% of organizations are actively taking steps to control observability costs, with 70% focused on optimizing existing spend rather than expanding.</p>
<p dir="auto"><strong>From above, AI is eating the intelligence layer.</strong> LLMs can write SQL. They can scan billions of log lines, correlate traces with metrics, perform root cause analysis, and define SLOs by analyzing historical patterns — all in seconds. They don't need dashboards, proprietary query languages, or pre-built visualizations. Give an LLM access to raw telemetry in an open format and a SQL interface, and it replicates what took observability platforms years and thousands of engineers to build.</p>
<p dir="auto">The emerging stack looks like this:</p>
<div class="snippet-clipboard-content notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="OpenTelemetry SDKs → Commodity columnar storage → AI agent"><pre class="notranslate"><code>OpenTelemetry SDKs → Commodity columnar storage → AI agent
</code></pre></div>
<p dir="auto">Everything in between — the dashboards, the query builders, the alert rule editors, the visualization layers — becomes optional middleware. Not immediately worthless, but structurally threatened.</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h3 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">What gets replaced</h3><a id="user-content-what-gets-replaced" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: What gets replaced" href="#what-gets-replaced"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">Traditional observability platforms provide value through:</p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li><strong>Dashboards</strong> → AI generates purpose-built visualizations on demand, used for a single investigation, then discarded. Persistent dashboards are artifacts of human cognitive limitation, not engineering necessity.</li>
<li><strong>Query languages</strong> → AI writes SQL (or whatever the storage engine speaks). Proprietary query languages like LogQL, PromQL, and SPL become friction, not features.</li>
<li><strong>Alert rules</strong> → AI performs continuous inference against raw data, identifying anomalies contextually rather than through static thresholds that humans forgot to update.</li>
<li><strong>Root cause analysis</strong> → AI traces causality across all three signal types natively, joining traces to logs to metrics without requiring humans to manually correlate.</li>
<li><strong>SLO definition</strong> → AI analyzes historical patterns, understands user impact, and sets thresholds that actually reflect system behavior rather than guesses.</li>
</ul>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h3 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">What remains</h3><a id="user-content-what-remains" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: What remains" href="#what-remains"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">Ingest and store. That's it. You need something to receive telemetry and something to persist it in a queryable format. Everything above that layer is intelligence — and intelligence is exactly what LLMs do.</p>
<p dir="auto"><strong>ducktel is a proof of concept for this thesis.</strong> It is the minimal backend an AI agent needs to do observability: receive OTLP, write Parquet, expose SQL. No dashboards. No query language. No visualization engine. Just structured data and a query interface that any LLM can use by shelling out to a CLI.</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Design Principles</h2><a id="user-content-design-principles" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Design Principles" href="#design-principles"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto"><strong>OTel-native.</strong> ducktel speaks OTLP/HTTP natively — both protobuf and JSON. No proprietary agents, no custom SDKs, no vendor lock-in at the collection layer. If your application is instrumented with OpenTelemetry, ducktel accepts it unchanged.</p>
<p dir="auto"><strong>Parquet-first storage.</strong> Telemetry is flushed to date-partitioned Parquet files. Parquet is columnar, compressed, and universally supported. DuckDB, Spark, Pandas, Polars, and dozens of other tools can read it natively. Your data never gets trapped in a proprietary format.</p>
<p dir="auto"><strong>SQL is the interface.</strong> Every query goes through DuckDB's SQL engine. This is a deliberate choice — SQL is the most widely understood query language on earth, and more importantly, it's the language LLMs are best at generating. No proprietary DSL to learn, no query builder to click through.</p>
<p dir="auto"><strong>CLI-first, agent-friendly.</strong> ducktel is designed to be called from a shell. An LLM agent investigating an incident can shell out to <code>ducktel query</code>, get structured JSON back, reason about the results, and issue follow-up queries. The entire diagnostic loop — from anomaly detection to root cause analysis — can happen programmatically without a human touching a browser.</p>
<p dir="auto"><strong>Single binary, zero dependencies.</strong> <code>go build</code> and you have everything. No databases to run, no message queues to configure, no clusters to manage. This matters for local development, CI/CD pipelines, edge deployments, and anywhere you want telemetry without the overhead of a platform.</p>
<p dir="auto"><strong>Nothing is dropped.</strong> All OTLP fields are preserved in the Parquet schema. Resource attributes, scope metadata, span events, links, exemplars — everything. The schema is wide because the data model is rich, and AI agents can use all of it.</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Architecture</h2><a id="user-content-architecture" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Architecture" href="#architecture"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>

<div class="highlight highlight-source-shell notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" dir="auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="ducktel serve"><pre>ducktel serve</pre></div>
<p dir="auto">Listens on <code>:4318</code> for OTLP/HTTP (protobuf and JSON). Accepts all three signal types:</p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li><code>POST /v1/traces</code></li>
<li><code>POST /v1/logs</code></li>
<li><code>POST /v1/metrics</code></li>
</ul>
<p dir="auto">Data is buffered in memory and flushed to Parquet files under <code>./data/{traces,logs,metrics}/YYYY-MM-DD/</code>.</p>
<p dir="auto">Options:</p>
<div class="snippet-clipboard-content notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="--port            Port to listen on (default 4318)
--flush-interval  How often to flush to disk (default 30s)
--data-dir        Storage directory (default ./data)"><pre class="notranslate"><code>--port            Port to listen on (default 4318)
--flush-interval  How often to flush to disk (default 30s)
--data-dir        Storage directory (default ./data)
</code></pre></div>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h3 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Query with SQL</h3><a id="user-content-query-with-sql" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Query with SQL" href="#query-with-sql"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">Run arbitrary SQL against any signal type:</p>
<div class="highlight highlight-source-shell notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" dir="auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="ducktel query "SELECT service_name, span_name, duration_ms FROM traces ORDER BY duration_ms DESC LIMIT 10"

<p dir="auto">Saved queries are the LLM's checklist — queries worth running periodically. ducktel stores them but never executes them automatically. There is no scheduler, no webhook, no notification system. The LLM agent decides when to run them (on its own heartbeat loop, cron, or whenever it wants) and what to do with the results.</p>
<div class="highlight highlight-source-shell notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" dir="auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="# Save a query the agent discovered during an investigation
ducktel saved create "error-rate-by-service" \
  "SELECT service_name, count(*) FILTER (WHERE status_code = 'STATUS_CODE_ERROR') * 100.0 / count(*) as error_pct FROM traces WHERE start_time >= epoch_us(now() - INTERVAL '5 minutes') GROUP BY service_name HAVING error_pct > 0" \
  --description "Error rate by service over last 5 minutes" \
  --schedule "every 60s" \
  --tags errors,slo

# Save a latency check
ducktel saved create "p99-latency" \
  "SELECT service_name, span_name, quantile_cont(duration_ms, 0.99) as p99_ms FROM traces WHERE start_time >= epoch_us(now() - INTERVAL '10 minutes') GROUP BY service_name, span_name ORDER BY p99_ms DESC LIMIT 10" \
  --description "Top 10 slowest endpoints by P99 latency" \
  --schedule "every 5m" \
  --tags latency

# List all saved queries
ducktel saved list
ducktel saved list --format json

# Show a specific query's details
ducktel saved show "error-rate-by-service"

# Run a single saved query
ducktel saved run "error-rate-by-service"

# Run ALL saved queries at once — the agent's heartbeat check
# One command, all diagnostics, structured JSON output
ducktel saved run-all

# Delete a query that's no longer relevant
ducktel saved delete "error-rate-by-service""><pre><span class="pl-c"><span class="pl-c">#</span> Save a query the agent discovered during an investigation</span>

  <span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">"</span>SELECT service_name, count(*) FILTER (WHERE status_code = 'STATUS_CODE_ERROR') * 100.0 / count(*) as error_pct FROM traces WHERE start_time >= epoch_us(now() - INTERVAL '5 minutes') GROUP BY service_name HAVING error_pct > 0<span class="pl-pds">"</span></span> \
  --description <span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">"</span>Error rate by service over last 5 minutes<span class="pl-pds">"</span></span> \

  --tags errors,slo

<span class="pl-c"><span class="pl-c">#</span> Save a latency check</span>
ducktel saved create <span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">"</span>p99-latency<span class="pl-pds">"</span></span> \
  <span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">"</span>SELECT service_name, span_name, quantile_cont(duration_ms, 0.99) as p99_ms FROM traces WHERE start_time >= epoch_us(now() - INTERVAL '10 minutes') GROUP BY service_name, span_name ORDER BY p99_ms DESC LIMIT 10<span class="pl-pds">"</span></span> \

<p dir="auto">The <code>run-all</code> command is the key primitive. An LLM agent on a heartbeat loop runs <code>ducktel saved run-all</code>, gets back a JSON array of all results, and reasons about what needs attention. The investigative query that found a bug today becomes the monitoring query that catches it tomorrow — no translation layer, no alert rule syntax, just SQL.</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Agent Integration</h2><a id="user-content-agent-integration" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Agent Integration" href="#agent-integration"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">ducktel is built for LLM agents. Here's how an agent might investigate an incident:</p>
<div class="highlight highlight-source-shell notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" dir="auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="# Step 1: What services are reporting?
ducktel services --format json

# Step 2: Any errors in the last hour?
ducktel query "
  SELECT service_name, count(*) as error_count
  FROM traces
  WHERE status_code = 'STATUS_CODE_ERROR'
    AND start_time >= epoch_us(now() - INTERVAL '1 hour')
  GROUP BY service_name
  ORDER BY error_count DESC
" --format json

# Step 3: What's failing in the worst service?
ducktel query "
  SELECT span_name, count(*) as failures, avg(duration_ms) as avg_duration
  FROM traces
  WHERE service_name = 'payment-service'
    AND status_code = 'STATUS_CODE_ERROR'
    AND start_time >= epoch_us(now() - INTERVAL '1 hour')
  GROUP BY span_name
  ORDER BY failures DESC
" --format json

# Step 4: Get a specific failing trace
ducktel query "
  SELECT span_name, parent_span_id, duration_ms, status_code, attributes
  FROM traces
  WHERE trace_id = '...'
  ORDER BY start_time
" --format json

# Step 5: Correlate with logs
ducktel query "
  SELECT timestamp, severity_text, body
  FROM logs
  WHERE trace_id = '...'
  ORDER BY timestamp
" --format json

# Step 6: Check if this is a latency regression
ducktel query "
  SELECT metric_name, service_name,
         sum / count as avg_ms, max as max_ms
  FROM metrics
  WHERE metric_name = 'http.request.duration'
    AND service_name = 'payment-service'
  ORDER BY timestamp DESC
  LIMIT 20
" --format json"><pre><span class="pl-c"><span class="pl-c">#</span> Step 1: What services are reporting?</span>
ducktel services --format json

<span class="pl-c"><span class="pl-c">#</span> Step 2: Any errors in the last hour?</span>

<span class="pl-s">  SELECT service_name, count(*) as error_count</span>
<span class="pl-s">  FROM traces</span>
<span class="pl-s">  WHERE status_code = 'STATUS_CODE_ERROR'</span>
<span class="pl-s">    AND start_time >= epoch_us(now() - INTERVAL '1 hour')</span>
<span class="pl-s">  GROUP BY service_name</span>
<span class="pl-s">  ORDER BY error_count DESC</span>
<span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">"</span></span> --format json

<span class="pl-c"><span class="pl-c">#</span> Step 3: What's failing in the worst service?</span>

<span class="pl-s">  ORDER BY failures DESC</span>

<span class="pl-c"><span class="pl-c">#</span> Step 4: Get a specific failing trace</span>

<span class="pl-s">  FROM traces</span>
<span class="pl-s">  WHERE trace_id = '...'</span>

<span class="pl-s">  SELECT timestamp, severity_text, body</span>
<span class="pl-s">  FROM logs</span>
<span class="pl-s">  WHERE trace_id = '...'</span>
<span class="pl-s">  ORDER BY timestamp</span>

<span class="pl-c"><span class="pl-c">#</span> Step 6: Check if this is a latency regression</span>

<span class="pl-s">  SELECT metric_name, service_name,</span>
<span class="pl-s">         sum / count as avg_ms, max as max_ms</span>
<span class="pl-s">  FROM metrics</span>
<span class="pl-s">  WHERE metric_name = 'http.request.duration'</span>
<span class="pl-s">    AND service_name = 'payment-service'</span>

<p dir="auto">Every step returns structured JSON. The agent reasons about each result and decides what to query next. No dashboards opened. No humans clicking through UIs. No context-switching between tabs. Just an AI systematically narrowing from "something's wrong" to "here's the root cause and here's the evidence."</p>
<p dir="auto">This is what observability looks like when the consumer of telemetry is an LLM, not a human staring at a screen.</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h3 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">The diagnostic-to-monitoring loop</h3><a id="user-content-the-diagnostic-to-monitoring-loop" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: The diagnostic-to-monitoring loop" href="#the-diagnostic-to-monitoring-loop"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">The real power of saved queries: the investigative query that diagnosed an incident becomes the monitoring query that prevents the next one. No context switch, no "now go create an alert rule in a different system."</p>
<div class="highlight highlight-source-shell notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" dir="auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="# Agent just diagnosed a payment service issue. Save the query that found it:
ducktel saved create "payment-error-spike" \
  "SELECT count(*) as errors FROM traces WHERE service_name = 'payment-service' AND status_code = 'STATUS_CODE_ERROR' AND start_time >= epoch_us(now() - INTERVAL '5 minutes')" \
  --description "Errors in payment service over 5min window" \
  --schedule "every 60s" \
  --tags payment,errors

# Later, on the agent's heartbeat loop:
ducktel saved run-all
# → Agent sees payment-error-spike returned 0 rows. All clear.
# → Next heartbeat, it returns 47 rows. Agent investigates."><pre><span class="pl-c"><span class="pl-c">#</span> Agent just diagnosed a payment service issue. Save the query that found it:</span>
ducktel saved create <span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">"</span>payment-error-spike<span class="pl-pds">"</span></span> \
  <span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">"</span>SELECT count(*) as errors FROM traces WHERE service_name = 'payment-service' AND status_code = 'STATUS_CODE_ERROR' AND start_time >= epoch_us(now() - INTERVAL '5 minutes')<span class="pl-pds">"</span></span> \
  --description <span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">"</span>Errors in payment service over 5min window<span class="pl-pds">"</span></span> \
  --schedule <span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">"</span>every 60s<span class="pl-pds">"</span></span> \
  --tags payment,errors

<span class="pl-c"><span class="pl-c">#</span> Later, on the agent's heartbeat loop:</span>
ducktel saved run-all
<span class="pl-c"><span class="pl-c">#</span> → Agent sees payment-error-spike returned 0 rows. All clear.</span>
<span class="pl-c"><span class="pl-c">#</span> → Next heartbeat, it returns 47 rows. Agent investigates.</span></pre></div>

<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Example Queries</h2><a id="user-content-example-queries" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Example Queries" href="#example-queries"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<div class="highlight highlight-source-sql notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" dir="auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="-- Slowest spans in the last hour
SELECT service_name, span_name, duration_ms
FROM traces
WHERE start_time >= epoch_us(now() - INTERVAL '1 hour')
ORDER BY duration_ms DESC
LIMIT 10;

-- Error rate by service
SELECT service_name,
       count(*) as total,
       count(*) FILTER (WHERE status_code = 'STATUS_CODE_ERROR') as errors
FROM traces
GROUP BY service_name;

-- Trace waterfall
SELECT span_name, parent_span_id, duration_ms,
       start_time - min(start_time) OVER (PARTITION BY trace_id) as offset_us
FROM traces
WHERE trace_id = '01020304050607080910111213141516'
ORDER BY start_time;

-- Recent error logs
SELECT timestamp, service_name, body
FROM logs
WHERE severity_text = 'ERROR'
ORDER BY timestamp DESC
LIMIT 20;

-- Logs correlated with a trace
SELECT severity_text, body
FROM logs
WHERE trace_id = '01020304050607080910111213141516'
ORDER BY timestamp;

-- P99 request duration from histograms
SELECT metric_name, service_name,
       sum / count as avg_ms,
       max as max_ms
FROM metrics
WHERE metric_name = 'http.request.duration'
ORDER BY timestamp DESC
LIMIT 10;

-- Cross-signal: find error spans and their logs
SELECT t.span_name, t.duration_ms, l.body
FROM traces t
JOIN logs l ON t.trace_id = l.trace_id AND t.span_id = l.span_id
WHERE t.status_code = 'STATUS_CODE_ERROR'
ORDER BY t.start_time DESC;"><pre><span class="pl-c"><span class="pl-c">--</span> Slowest spans in the last hour</span>
<span class="pl-k">SELECT</span> service_name, span_name, duration_ms
<span class="pl-k">FROM</span> traces
<span class="pl-k">WHERE</span> start_time <span class="pl-k">>=</span> epoch_us(now() <span class="pl-k">-</span> INTERVAL <span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">'</span>1 hour<span class="pl-pds">'</span></span>)
<span class="pl-k">ORDER BY</span> duration_ms <span class="pl-k">DESC</span>
<span class="pl-k">LIMIT</span> <span class="pl-c1">10</span>;

<span class="pl-c"><span class="pl-c">--</span> Error rate by service</span>
<span class="pl-k">SELECT</span> service_name,
       <span class="pl-c1">count</span>(<span class="pl-k">*</span>) <span class="pl-k">as</span> total,
       <span class="pl-c1">count</span>(<span class="pl-k">*</span>) FILTER (<span class="pl-k">WHERE</span> status_code <span class="pl-k">=</span> <span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">'</span>STATUS_CODE_ERROR<span class="pl-pds">'</span></span>) <span class="pl-k">as</span> errors
<span class="pl-k">FROM</span> traces
<span class="pl-k">GROUP BY</span> service_name;

<span class="pl-c"><span class="pl-c">--</span> Trace waterfall</span>
<span class="pl-k">SELECT</span> span_name, parent_span_id, duration_ms,
       start_time <span class="pl-k">-</span> <span class="pl-c1">min</span>(start_time) OVER (PARTITION BY trace_id) <span class="pl-k">as</span> offset_us
<span class="pl-k">FROM</span> traces
<span class="pl-k">WHERE</span> trace_id <span class="pl-k">=</span> <span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">'</span>01020304050607080910111213141516<span class="pl-pds">'</span></span>
<span class="pl-k">ORDER BY</span> start_time;

<span class="pl-c"><span class="pl-c">--</span> Recent error logs</span>
<span class="pl-k">SELECT</span> <span class="pl-k">timestamp</span>, service_name, body
<span class="pl-k">FROM</span> logs
<span class="pl-k">WHERE</span> severity_text <span class="pl-k">=</span> <span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">'</span>ERROR<span class="pl-pds">'</span></span>
<span class="pl-k">ORDER BY</span> <span class="pl-k">timestamp</span> <span class="pl-k">DESC</span>
<span class="pl-k">LIMIT</span> <span class="pl-c1">20</span>;

<span class="pl-c"><span class="pl-c">--</span> Logs correlated with a trace</span>
<span class="pl-k">SELECT</span> severity_text, body
<span class="pl-k">FROM</span> logs
<span class="pl-k">WHERE</span> trace_id <span class="pl-k">=</span> <span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">'</span>01020304050607080910111213141516<span class="pl-pds">'</span></span>
<span class="pl-k">ORDER BY</span> <span class="pl-k">timestamp</span>;

<span class="pl-c"><span class="pl-c">--</span> P99 request duration from histograms</span>
<span class="pl-k">SELECT</span> metric_name, service_name,
       sum <span class="pl-k">/</span> count <span class="pl-k">as</span> avg_ms,
       max <span class="pl-k">as</span> max_ms
<span class="pl-k">FROM</span> metrics
<span class="pl-k">WHERE</span> metric_name <span class="pl-k">=</span> <span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">'</span>http.request.duration<span class="pl-pds">'</span></span>
<span class="pl-k">ORDER BY</span> <span class="pl-k">timestamp</span> <span class="pl-k">DESC</span>
<span class="pl-k">LIMIT</span> <span class="pl-c1">10</span>;

<span class="pl-c"><span class="pl-c">--</span> Cross-signal: find error spans and their logs</span>
<span class="pl-k">SELECT</span> <span class="pl-c1">t</span>.<span class="pl-c1">span_name</span>, <span class="pl-c1">t</span>.<span class="pl-c1">duration_ms</span>, <span class="pl-c1">l</span>.<span class="pl-c1">body</span>
<span class="pl-k">FROM</span> traces t
<span class="pl-k">JOIN</span> logs l <span class="pl-k">ON</span> <span class="pl-c1">t</span>.<span class="pl-c1">trace_id</span> <span class="pl-k">=</span> <span class="pl-c1">l</span>.<span class="pl-c1">trace_id</span> <span class="pl-k">AND</span> <span class="pl-c1">t</span>.<span class="pl-c1">span_id</span> <span class="pl-k">=</span> <span class="pl-c1">l</span>.<span class="pl-c1">span_id</span>
<span class="pl-k">WHERE</span> <span class="pl-c1">t</span>.<span class="pl-c1">status_code</span> <span class="pl-k">=</span> <span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">'</span>STATUS_CODE_ERROR<span class="pl-pds">'</span></span>
<span class="pl-k">ORDER BY</span> <span class="pl-c1">t</span>.<span class="pl-c1">start_time</span> <span class="pl-k">DESC</span>;</pre></div>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">The Bigger Picture</h2><a id="user-content-the-bigger-picture" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: The Bigger Picture" href="#the-bigger-picture"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">ducktel isn't trying to be Datadog. It's not trying to be Grafana. It's not trying to be a platform at all.</p>
<p dir="auto">It's an answer to a question: *What's the minimum viable backend when the consumer of telemetry is an AI agent instead of a human?</p>
<p dir="auto">The answer turns out to be surprisingly small. An OTLP receiver, a Parquet writer, and a SQL engine. That's the whole thing. Everything observability platforms spent a decade building on top of that foundation — the dashboards, the query builders, the alerting engines, the visualization layers — was scaffolding for human cognition. Necessary scaffolding, when humans were the ones interpreting telemetry. But scaffolding nonetheless.</p>
<p dir="auto">When an LLM can write SQL, read structured output, reason about distributed systems, and iterate on queries faster than any human can click through a UI — the scaffolding becomes overhead.</p>
<p dir="auto">This isn't a prediction about the distant future. The pieces exist today. OpenTelemetry standardized collection. Parquet and DuckDB commoditized storage and query. LLMs can do the reasoning. ducktel just wires them together in the simplest possible way and gets out of the road.</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Status</h2><a id="user-content-status" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Status" href="#status"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">Early stage. The core ingest → store → query loop works. Contributions welcome.</p>
